newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur CEO details CS ties.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur CEO details CS ties.

text.p: Peter Spaetli, chief executive of Winterthur Insurance Co, said the appointment of Thomas Wellauer as new CEO at the insurer did not necessarily mean Winterthur would seek equity ties to Credit Suisse (CS) group.

"The appointment of Mr. Wellauer will not lead per se to a closer relationship with CS Group, led by Lukas Muehlemann. The secret of a successful cooperation lies in a clear committment at the top, and its execution in both organisations. For that, one does not need equity capital links," Spaetli said in an interview published in Saturday's edition of Finanz und Wirtschaft.
"Further developments in the cooperation will be determined by needs and opportunities offered by the markets," he added.
Wellauer will take the key executive position at Winterthur starting January 1, 1998.
Wellauer, like new CS chief executive Lukas Muehlemann, has worked for consultancy firm McKinsey.
Winterthur said when Wellauer's appointment was announced last week that he most recently was a corporate consultant at McKinsey, charged with Winterthur and its partner CS Group.
Muehlemann moved to banking group CS from Swiss Reinsurance last year. He joined Swiss Re in 1994, leaving his position McKinsey and Co, Switzerland where he was managing director.
Winterthur and CS agreed in December 1995 to cooperate in a joint venture involving sale of banking and insurance products.
Spaetli also said that recent strong gains in Winterthur's share price may lie partly in market perception that its shares were "strongly undervalued."

He said that share purchases had been widely spread among investors, adding that at the end of 1996 when Winterthur published its most recent annual report, "no-one was in the realm of five percent" in terms of share holdings. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41 1 631 7340
